Researchers in deep learning also don’t understand why deep learning works. If we did understand how it and why it works then we would have made significant progress as to how the mind works.

To explore just how little we really know as to how deep learning works, let us explore some of the known limitations.

Adversarial features.

The largest flaw is the discovery that by tweaking an input image in a specific way one can fool a Deep Learning Neural Network to misclassify. This is a problem for not only deep learning but for almost every machine learning method that employ linear algebra to approximate its classifications. This is a major problem because the brain does not make this same kind of misclassification and it is an obvious limitation of deep learning systems that employ linear matching methods. The real tell here is, we don’t know of alternatives that will fix the problem!

Secondary to this flaw is the requirement for a large labeled training size to learn new concepts. We don’t know the minimum number of training examples needed to get a certain level of accuracy. All we know is, the more the better!

Third is the lack of interpretability of the models that are learned. We are in complete loss as to how we can even interpret the models learned by deep learning system.

Fourth is the limitation that any machine learning classification algorithm that is learning from data is only limited to identifying the cause given the observed effects. These systems have limits in their ability to predict behavior of other complex systems. That is, to predict the effect given an cause. In the category of computationally irreducible system, we don’t know which kinds a deep learning network can mimic well enough.

Fifth is the inability to perform unsupervised learning with the exception of Autoencoders. We just don’t know how to do unsupervised learning with deep learning.

In summary, research scientists themselves don’t know how it works!
